newsitem.title: CROATIA: IMF postpones $40 mln loan to Croatia - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: IMF postpones $40 mln loan to Croatia - c.bank.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) indefinitely postponed the $40 million second tranche of a three-year loan programme to Croatia, the central bank (NBH) said in a statement on Friday.
But the postponement would not seriously affect Croatia's liquidity, as the country's foreign exchange reserves of $4.7 billion roughly equalled its foreign debt, said the NBH's statement.
"The denial of the expected tranche will not have a direct significant impact on financial conditions of Croatia," the statement said.
The loan was intended to boost Croatia's international liquidity, it said. "(But) Croatia's foreign reserves amount to $2.4 billion in central bank's deposits and $2.3 billion with commercial banks.

"Together with the expected inflow of hard currency this summer, it is evident that the available reserves roughly amount to the entire foreign debt, which indicates a good level of international liquidity," the statement said.

The IMF and World Bank separately postponed discussing two Croatia loans in June and July, which had already been approved, following the U.S. pressure on Zagreb to comply with its peace committments or face financial isolation.
